name: make.par.list
title: Distribute a graphical parameter across series

origin.description: Build one parameter value per series from a vector or a partly named list.
origin.usage: make.par.list(nams, x, n, m, def, recycle = sum(unnamed) > 0)

arguments.name: nams
arguments.text: Series names. The result has one element for each name, in this order.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A parameter specification. An atomic vector is split into elements when m is greater than 1, and wrapped as one element when m is 1. A list may mix named series with unnamed defaults, as in list(A = c(1, 2), c(3, 4)).

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Length of each series. A value whose length is not 1 is recycled to n. A length-1 value stays length 1.

arguments.name: m
arguments.text: Number of series. Only the distinction between 1 and more than 1 changes how an atomic x is split.

arguments.name: def
arguments.text: Value used for a series that is still unspecified when recycle is FALSE. NULL clears the list, so the names are dropped and the unspecified elements stay NULL.

arguments.name: recycle
arguments.text: TRUE recycles unnamed elements across unspecified series. FALSE writes those unnamed elements in order and fills the rest with def. The default is TRUE when x has at least one unnamed element.

origin.details: Named elements are copied onto the series of the same name. With recycle TRUE and no unnamed element, the function stops with sum(unnamed) > 0 is not TRUE. An empty numeric value is recycled to n as NA. NULL stays NULL.
origin.value: A named list of length m, or a blank-named list when def is NULL.
origin.example:
nams <- c("A", "B", "C")
y <- make.par.list(nams, list(A = c(1, 2), c(3, 4)), 5, 3, 1)
cat(paste(names(y)[1], paste(y[[1]], collapse = "|"), sep = ": "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Build one parameter value per series from a vector or a partly named list.
translation.usage: make_par_list(nams, x, n, m, def_=1, recycle=None)

arguments.name: nams
arguments.text: Series names. The result is a list of (name, value) pairs in this order.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A dict is an all-named list. A list of (name, value) pairs uses "" for an unnamed element. A nested list is an unnamed list. A flat list, a scalar, or an array is atomic and follows the m == 1 rule.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Length of each series. A value whose length is not 1 is recycled to n. A length-1 value stays length 1.

arguments.name: m
arguments.text: Number of series. Only the distinction between 1 and more than 1 changes how an atomic x is split.

arguments.name: def_
arguments.text: R's def. None clears the names, matching y[] <- NULL.

arguments.name: recycle
arguments.text: None uses the R default: true when x has an unnamed element. True with no unnamed element raises ValueError: sum(unnamed) > 0 is not TRUE.

translation.details: The first matching name is kept. A vector default is recycled across the series cells, with the same non-multiple warning as y[] <- def. An empty numeric array becomes NA repeated n times.
translation.value: A list of (name, value) pairs. After a NULL default the names are empty strings.
translation.example:
from zoo.plot import make_par_list
rows = make_par_list(["A", "B", "C"], [("A", [1, 2]), ("", [3, 4])], 5, 3, 1)
print("A: " + "|".join(str(v) for v in rows[0][1]))
